Independent replay: generate records from 5 by r←r+λ(r−1) up to p_15=47, count each residue in [p_k,p_{k+1}) for k=4,…,14, and iterate w_k=p_k w_{k−1}−s_k from (5,4); exact integer certificate reproduced
correctness.rationale: The prior turning-point recurrence starts at 5. A skipped prime would give a smaller integer greater than 1 coprime to r−1 than its least missing prime, impossible. Inside each length-P_n translate, λ(t+jP_n)=λ(t) for 0<t<P_n; at a block endpoint λ(jP_n)=p_{n+1} for 1≤j<p_{n+1}. Starting from 31 this gives exact copies and the residue recurrence because 6 divides P_n. The odd spacing and Bertrand's bound give s_k(a)<p_k/2, so e_n(a)=P_n∑_{k>n}s_k(a)/P_k lies in [0,1). For t complete primorial lengths the accumulated tail satisfies t e_n≤s_{n+1}+1, not an uncontrolled error per block. The prefix agrees with t w_n+C_a(u) for u≥p_{n+1}; below that it is constant except for the record at tP_n+1. Counting the endpoint at u=0 with that record excluded gives the displayed two-case discrepancy recurrence. Since s_{n+1}≤(p_{n+2}−p_{n+1})/2 and the gap is at least 2, E_n≤2p_{n+1} follows by induction, and the prime number theorem gives O(log X). An independent short recurrence reproduces P_14=13082761331670030 and w_14(1)−w_14(5)=379045337581045; the two tails differ by strictly less than 1, and 35 times the lower numerator minus P_14 is 183825483666510>0.
residual_risks: The replay certifies the finite numerators and rational comparisons, not the unbounded recurrence, discrepancy, or equivalence to turning points. Those rest on the proof and the prior characterization.

evidence: The squarefree theorem includes residues 1 and 5 modulo 6 and gives the same series. Its prefix error is O(P_{n−1}+p_{n+1}²) relative to the level n−1 approximant on P_n≤X<P_{n+1}. The shift theorem concerns two-point densities Q(t).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The squarefree theorem dominates density existence and adds irrationality, but its stated quantitative estimate does not give logarithmic discrepancy for all prefixes. A six-shift pair density is not the difference of one-point densities in classes 1 and 5. Both overlapping indexed records are later-dated; no external priority is inferred.

originality.rationale: Prior work has the aggregate density and the primorial mechanism. A distinct, later indexed theorem covers classwise density existence and the same series for a larger family; the signed enclosure can be read out of its general tail bound after a finite calculation. What survives these comparisons is the uniform classwise O(log X) discrepancy, which is much stronger than the indexed prefix estimate, together with its application to this exact biased pair of densities.
residual_risks: A sharper prefix estimate in other sequence or discrepancy literature may remain unlocated; a bounded search cannot rule it out. Broad density existence is explicitly shared, not claimed original on its own.

value.rationale: Modulo six is the natural first split because the record recurrence forces records into precisely its two reduced classes. The signed result resolves persistent asymmetry rather than describing a short numerical fluctuation, and the logarithmic absolute error makes that distinction quantitative for all cutoffs. The essential gain is that prefix error, not the number of digits in the finite enclosure.
residual_risks: The theorem does not show optimality or a lower bound for the order of discrepancy, and does not claim this sharp upper bound for every modulus.
